experiments.hypothesis: Injecting the maximum allowed 15 s latency will keep client requests below the 30 s timeout, so error_rate stays <5 % and alerts (e.g., speeding) still fire, merely delayed by ~15 s.
experiments.reason: Tests the extreme latency edge while still respecting client timeout, probing both error rate and alert delay.

experiments.hypothesis: With 8 s added latency, a telemetry record that should trigger a speeding alert will be observed in the API ~8 s later, confirming linear alert delay and no device_offline alerts.
experiments.reason: Mid‑range latency to verify that alert generation delay matches injected latency.

experiments.hypothesis: Adding 5 s latency raises observer data_age to ~5.5 s (baseline 0.54 s + 1 s interval + 5 s), still below any offline detection, keeping error_rate ≈0 % while delaying alerts by ~5 s.
experiments.reason: Lower latency to confirm linear relationship between added latency and data_age/alert delay without triggering errors.
